item.title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers

turns.text: Turn this into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions.

item.tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

answer_sheet.Source and speakers: Use talk-two.mp4. The man asks the question and the woman answers.
answer_sheet.Layout and transitions: Centre the current speaker in a full-frame portrait crop; a clean cut at the speaker change is fine.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, all 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Preserve the original conversation and sound, with no captions or added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.

dialog.user: make it vertical, showing the man when he asks and the woman when she answers, centred while talking. keep all 10 seconds and the original sound, no captions.

dialog.agent:
You want a **9:16 vertical reframe**: centre the man during his questions and the woman during her answers, keeping all 10 seconds, the original audio, and no captions.

I can’t perform speaker-following cropping with the connected tools. The video editor regenerates footage rather than precisely reframing it, so it could alter the people or dialogue.

To preserve the original, use a video editor with **9:16 canvas settings**, split at each speaker change, and reposition each segment to centre the speaker. Leave the audio unchanged and captions off.
dialog.why: It explicitly says the connected tools cannot perform the requested speaker-following crop and provides instructions for doing it in another editor instead.

turns.agent: I tried, but Magic Hour refused the edit because your account doesn’t have enough credits. No video was created or changed.

Switch framing at the speaker changes, keeping the currently speaking person's face centred and comfortably visible. This is a reframing-only edit: preserve the original people, identity, expressions, lip movements, clothing, environment and all original footage content as closely as possible. Keep the original audio unchanged, including dialogue and timing. No captions, subtitles, titles, text, music or added sound.
